'''''Ceanothus arboreus''''' is a species of [[Perennial plant|perennial]] [[shrub]] to small [[tree]] in the family [[Rhamnaceae]], commonly known as the '''feltleaf ceanothus''', '''island ceanothus''', and '''island mountain lilac'''.<ref name=calflora>[http://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-calrecnum=1764 Calflora: ''Ceanothus arboreus'']</ref><ref>[https://npgsweb.ars-grin.gov/gringlobal/taxonomydetail.aspx?9644  GRIN-Global Web v 1.9.6.2: taxonomy of ''Ceanothus arboreus'']</ref> It is the largest member of the California lilacs (the ''[[Ceanothus]]'' genus), and is characterized with glossy, dark green foliage that is adorned by pale blue to white flowers in bloom. It is endemic to the [[Channel Islands (California)|Channel Islands of California]] and [[Guadalupe Island]] in [[Mexico]],<ref name="rebman">{{Cite journal|last1=Rebman|first1=J. P.|last2=Gibson|first2=J.|last3=Rich|first3=K.|date=2016|title=Annotated checklist of the vascular plants of Baja California, Mexico|url=http://sdplantatlas.org/pdffiles/BajaChecklist2016.pdf|journal=San Diego Society of Natural History|volume=45|pages=241}}</ref> only being re-discovered on Guadalupe Island after the elimination of [[feral goat]]s.<ref name="Mendoza1">{{Cite journal|last1=Luna-Mendoza|first1=Luciana|last2=Aguirre-Muñoz|first2=Alfonso|last3=Hernández-Montoya|first3=J.C.|last4=Torres-Aguilar|first4=Marisol|last5=García-Carreón|first5=Jacinto|last6=Hernandez|first6=Orlando|last7=Luvianos-Colin|first7=Sergio|last8=Cárdenas|first8=Ana|last9=Méndez Sánchez|first9=Federico|date=2019|title=Ten years after feral goat eradication: the active restoration of plant communities on Guadalupe Island, Mexico|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331939753|journal=Occasional Paper SSC|volume=62|pages=571–575}}</ref>

==Description==
''Ceanothus arboreus'' is a spreading bush growing up to {{convert|12|-|36|ft|m}} in height.<ref name="jepson">[http://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/eflora/eflora_display.php?tid=18428 Jepson eFlora: ''Ceanothus arboreus'']</ref> It has large, glossy, dark green leaves which are leathery or felt-like on their undersides.<ref name=jepson/>

Its showy bright blue flowers grow in plentiful [[panicle]]s, or bunches, of tiny five-lobed blossoms.<ref name=jepson/> Some varieties and cultivars have light, powder purple blooms, and others bear darker purple flowers.  The bloom period is February to April.<ref name=calflora/>

The fruits are three-lobed, triangular capsules.<ref name=jepson/>

== Distribution ==
The plant is [[endemism|endemic]] to three of the [[Channel Islands (California)|Channel Islands of California]]: [[Santa Cruz Island]], [[Santa Rosa Island, California|Santa Rosa Island]], and [[Santa Catalina Island, California|Santa Catalina Island]],<ref name="calflora" /><ref name="jepson" /> and it is also found on [[Guadalupe Island]] in [[Mexico]].<ref name="rebman" />

It is found on slopes in [[coastal sage scrub]] and [[chaparral]] habitats.<ref name="calflora" />[[File:J20160218-0104—Ceanothus arboreus—RPBG (25237823956).jpg|thumb]]

==Cultivation==
'''Ceanothus arboreus'' is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]] for use in [[xeriscape|drought tolerant]] and [[wildlife garden]]s and [[natural landscaping]] projects.<ref name=laspilitas>[http://www.laspilitas.com/nature-of-california/plants/137--ceanothus-arboreus Las Pilitas Nursery Horticultural Database: ''Ceanothus arboreus'' (Tree Lilac, Island Mt. Lilac)]</ref><ref>[http://www.wildflower.org/plants/result.php?id_plant=CEAR Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center Native Plant Information Network−NPIN: ''Ceanothus arboreus''  (Feltleaf ceanothus, Island ceanothus, Island mountain lilac)]</ref>  Butterflies like the flowers and the quail eat the seeds.<ref name=laspilitas/>

===Cultivars===
Numerous [[cultivars]] have been selected for garden use, including:
* ''Ceanothus arboreus'' 'Cliff Schmidt' — more compact habit and deeper blue flowers.<ref>[http://www.yerbabuenanursery.com/viewplant.php?pid=1323Yerba Buena Nursery native plants database: ''Ceanothus arboreus'' 'Cliff Schmidt']</ref>
*''Ceanothus arboreus'' 'Owlswood Blue'.<ref>[http://www.laspilitas.com/groups/ceanothus/southern_california_lilacs/southern_california_lilacs.html Las Pilitas Nursery Horticultural Database: Southern California Lilacs, Ceanothus spp. and cultivars.]</ref>
*''Ceanothus arboreus'' 'Powder Blue' — Powder Blue Ceanothus, Compact Feltleaf Ceanothus.<ref>[http://www.smgrowers.com/products/plants/plantdisplay.asp?plant_id=2506 San Marcos Growers Horticulture Database: ''Ceanothus arboreus'' 'Powder Blue']</ref><ref>[https://www.sbbg.org/sites/default/files/pdfs/Branching%20out_ceanothus_powder_blue.pdf  The Santa Barbara Botanic Garden.org: Ceanothus 'Powder Blue' ] — ''with images''.</ref><ref>[http://www.yerbabuenanursery.com/viewplant.php?pid=1576  Yerba Buena Nursery native plants database: ''Ceanothus arboreus'' 'Powder Blue']</ref>
*''Ceanothus arboreus'' 'Skylark' 
*''Ceanothus arboreus'' 'Trewithen Blue' — very dark blue flowered form from the Channel Islands.<ref>[http://www.yerbabuenanursery.com/viewplant.php?pid=1176 Yerba Buena Nursery native plants database: ''Ceanothus arboreus'' 'Trewithen Blue']</ref>  It has received the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Ceanothus arboreus'' 'Trewithen Blue'|url=
https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/3253/Ceanothus-arboreus-Trewithen-Blue/Details | accessdate=15 April 2020}}</ref>
